public_rationale: OpenAI's January 18, 2026 disclosure describes consumer subscriptions, workplace subscriptions, APIs, and commerce [e1]. The existence of these channels does not establish that OpenAI can reach the revenue target without sustained growth from big-business customers [e1]. The disclosure establishes neither the absence of that growth nor achievement of the annual revenue target or irreversible cessation of the business, so it does not settle the forecast early [e1].
limitations: The contract's December 31, 2030 deadline is after the October 28, 2026 evaluation date.
The evidence lacks a consistently defined big-business revenue series through the forecast period and the 2030 realized annual revenue outcome.
The contract uses approximately $200 billion in realized annual revenue for calendar 2030; the source leaves the precise target, customer scope, and required growth ambiguous.
A target miss alone would not support the conditional forecast; the absence of sustained big-business revenue growth must also be established.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI cannot reach its ambitious revenue numbers (13x-ing current revenue in five years) unless revenue from paying big business customers keeps going up.
conditions: unless revenue from paying big business customers keeps going up

statement.excerpt: Needless to say, OpenAI can’t make its ambitious revenue numbers — 13x-ing current revenue in five years — unless revenue from paying big business customers keeps going up and up and up and up and up.

from_speaker: can’t make its ambitious revenue numbers
unless revenue from paying big business customers keeps going up
our_interpretation: Read the statement as a necessary-condition forecast: if large-business revenue does not keep growing, OpenAI will not reach the stated total-revenue target.
The conditional antecedent is failure of sustained large-business revenue growth, not the occurrence of growth.
Use approximately $200 billion in realized annual revenue during calendar 2030 as the target supplied by the surrounding passage.
Use December 31, 2030 as the latest deadline permitted by the named year.
Interpret repeated 'going up' as sustained growth across the forecast period, rather than growth every day or month.
The financial target is a press-reported estimate, not a specified GAAP measure.
criteria.support_condition: If the absence of sustained large-business revenue growth is established, OpenAI falls short of approximately $200 billion in realized annual revenue in 2030.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI achieves approximately $200 billion in realized annual revenue by the deadline despite an established absence of sustained large-business revenue growth.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable total and big-business revenue records through 2030 would establish whether the condition occurred and the target was reached. If sustained big-business revenue growth is absent, falling short of approximately $200 billion in realized annual revenue in 2030 would support the forecast; reaching it would contradict it. Early contradiction requires documented achievement of the annual revenue target without sustained big-business growth. Early support requires irreversible cessation of OpenAI's revenue-generating business, with the absence of sustained big-business growth independently
